__
 
• **CO₂ **is a by-product of cellular **respiration **in living organisms.
 
• CO₂ produced during respiration increases the **volume of air in the lungs**, this is known as **hyperventilation**.
 
• **Hyperventilation **occurs when an individual breathes faster or deeper than normal.
 
• **Hyperventilation **can lead to a decrease in the amount of** CO2 in the blood.**
 
• This decrease in CO2 can cause symptoms such as **lightheadedness.**
 
• Hyperventilation can also cause other symptoms** such as tingling in the fingers and mouth, muscle spasms, and shortness of breath.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• During normal breathing, carbon dioxide (CO₂) is produced as **a waste product of metabolism.**
 
• CO2 is carried by the blood to the lungs, where it is **exhaled**.
 
• In the lungs,** CO2 acts as a respiratory stimulant**, which helps to regulate the rate and depth of breathing.
 
• The CO2 level in the blood is closely regulated to maintain a balance between **the amount produced and the amount exhaled.**
 
• When the level of CO2 in the blood is too high, it can cause an increase in the **volume of air in the lungs**, which is known as **hyperventilation**.
 
• **Hyperventilation **can also be caused by** anxiety, panic attacks, and other emotional disturbances.**
 
• Hyperventilation can be treated by various methods,** such as breathing exercises, to help regulate the breathing rate and decrease the volume of air in the lungs.**

questions.question: The compound interest earned in 1 year on ₹40,000 at the rate of 40% per annum, compounded quarterly, is:

r = Rate of interest

t = time in years

n = Number of times the amount is compounding.

As it is compounded quarterly, so n = 4

⇒ CI = 40000times ((11)/(10))⁴ – 40000

⇒ CI = 40000times (121)/(100)times (121)/(100) – 40000

questions.question: A 4 Ω resistor, A, is connected in series to a 6 Ω resistor, B, and a 2 V battery. The potential drops across A and B are respectively ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4)0.8 V and 1.2 V**

**Given:**

R1=4Ω,R2=6Ω

Voltage, V=2V

**Formula:**

The potential drop of individual resistors are connected in series can be found by the formulas:

V1={R1over(R1+R2)}*V

V2={R2over(R1+R2)}*V

**Calculations:**

The potential drop at A is:

V1={R1over(R1+R2)}*V

V1={4over(4+6)}*2={4over10}*2=0.8V

The potential drop at B is:

V2={R2over(R1+R2)}*V

V2={6over(4+6)}*2={6over10}*2=1.2V

Therefore, the potential drops across A and B are **0.8 V and 1.2 V.**

questions.question: The HCF of (x⁴ − y⁴), (x⁸ − y⁸) and (x² − y²) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(x4 − y4), (x8 − y8) and (x2 − y2)

**Concept Used:**

HCF is the highest common factor in each of the terms to divide it completely.

a² – b² = (a + b)(a – b)

**Calculation:**

Factorizing each of the terms,

⇒ x8 − y⁸ 

= (x⁴ + y⁴)(x⁴ – y⁴) 

= (x4 + y4)(x² + y²)(x² – y²)

⇒ x8 − y8 = (x4 + y4)(x2 + y2)(x + y)(x – y)

For the second term,

⇒ x4 − y⁴ 

= (x2 + y2)(x2 – y2)

⇒ x4 − y4 = (x2 + y2)(x + y)(x – y)

For the third term,

⇒ x2 − y² = (x + y)(x – y)

In all the prime factorizations, the common factor is (x + y)(x – y).

**Therefore, the HCF of (x4 − y4), (x8 − y8) and (x2 − y2) is (x + y)(x ****– y).**

questions.solution:

__
 
• The stimulating **impacts **of **governmental **or **private investments **are referred to as the **investment multiplier.**
 
• It is based on **John Maynard Keynes'** economic **theories**.
 
• The **marginal propensity to save (MPS) **and the** marginal propensity to consume (MPC) **determine the size of the investment multiplier (MPS).
 
• An investment's potential to stimulate the economy more strongly is indicated by a **higher investment multiplier. **

• **Depending** on **income**, MPC **fluctuates**.
 
• MPC **tends **to be **lower **at **higher income levels.**
 
• The **Keynesian multiplier**, which describes the impact of the additional investment or government spending as an economic stimulus, is mostly determined by MPC.

questions.question: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror at a point beyond its centre of curvature C. The image is formed at a point ______ and is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** between F and C, diminished**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• An object is placed in front of a concave mirror at a point beyond its centre of curvature C, the image is formed at a point that is between the** centre of curvature and the focus (C and F respectively)**,__ and is real, inverted and smaller than the object.
 
• When an object is placed at a point beyond the centre of curvature of a concave mirror, the reflected rays converge at a point before the mirror,** creating a real image that is inverted and smaller than the object**. The image is also located between the** centre of curvature and the focus** of the mirror.
 
• It's also worth noting that in this case, the image is also always virtual, since the image is formed "**behind**" the mirror, meaning that it cannot be projected on a screen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When an object is placed at a point beyond the centre of curvature (C) of a concave mirror, the reflected rays converge at a point before the mirror, creating **a real image that is inverted (upside-down) and smaller than the object**. The image is also located between the centre of **curvature and the focus (F) of the mirror.**
 
• Additionally, it is also worth noting that the **distance of the object (u), the distance of the image (v), and the focal length (f) **of the mirror are related by the mirror equation:
 
• **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**
 
• Where, a negative value of v represents that the image is real, inverted and on the same side of the mirror as the object, and** a positive value of v** represents that** the image is virtual, erect and on the opposite side of the mirror.**
 
• Also, The image is always** diminished in size as the object is beyond the centre of curvature of the mirror**, The image is also always **virtual**, since the image is formed "**behind**" the mirror, meaning that it cannot be projected on a screen.

questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 24 and 456, respectively. If one number is 96, then the other number is:
questions.solution:

HCF of two numbers = 24

LCM of two numbers = 456

One number = 96

**Concept Used:**

LCM × HCF = Product of two numbers

**Calculation:**

Let the second number be x.

Putting the values, we get

⇒ 24 × 456 = 96 × x

⇒ x = (24times 456)/(96) = (456)/(4) = 114

Hence, the other number is** 114.**

questions.question: A decomposition reaction carried out by heating is called ________________.

__
 
• **Thermal Decomposition**

 
 
• **A decomposition reaction carried out by heating is called thermal decomposition.**
 
• **Thermolysis**, also known as **thermal decomposition, **is a chemical decomposition brought on by heat.
 
• The **decomposition temperature** of a substance is the temperature at which the substance begins to chemically break down.
 
• The process is often **endothermic** because heat is required to break the **chemical bonds** in the substance that is being broken down.
 
• A **positive feedback** loop that results in thermal runaway and maybe an explosion or other chemical event is formed if decomposition is **sufficiently exothermic**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition Reaction**

 
 
• One reactant produces two or more products in a **decomposition reaction.**
 
• A decomposition Reaction** is a type of chemical reaction.**
 
• **Chemical breakdowns or analysis reactions **are other names for decomposition processes.
 
• **Synthesis**, which involves the combination of less **complex reactants** to create a more complex result, is the reverse of this kind of reaction.
 
• **Hydrogen gas and oxygen gas **can be produced from water by **electrolysis through a decomposition reaction.**

Product of their ages = 6300

**Calculation:**

Let the father's age be 7x and the son's age be 4x.

According to the question,

⇒ 7x × 4x = 6300

questions.question: Which amendments of the Constitution of India aimed at strengthening local governments and ensuring an element of uniformity in their structure and functioning across the country?

__
 
• **Amendments to the Constitution**

 
 
• **​**There are** three kinds** of amendments to the Indian Constitution that are mentioned in **Article 368**. There are three types of amendments: those approved by a **special majority of the Parliament** (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), and those approved by a **special majority of the Parliament** and** ratified by half of the states**.
 
• The following is a list of the various kinds of amendments. The Constitution is able to be changed in three ways:
 
 
• **Amendment by a simple majority of the Parliament**: Outside of the scope of Article 368, a simple majority of the two houses of Parliament is required to amend a number of Constitutional provisions. Among** these provisions** are:
 
 
• new states' admission or establishment
 
• alterations to existing states' areas, borders, and names as well as the creation of new states.
 
• state legislative councils being abolished or created.
 
• Second Schedule: the president, governors, Speakers, judges, and other high-ranking officials' perks and allowances.
 
• In Parliament, quorum.
 
• allowances and salaries for Parliamentary members.
 
 
 
• **Amendment by a special majority of the Parliament**
 
 
• A special majority of Parliament—that is, a majority of **more than 50% **of the total members of each House and a majority of two-thirds of the members of each House who are present and voting—is required to amend the majority of the Constitution's provisions. The term **"total membership" **refers to the total number of House members, regardless of whether there are vacancies or absentees.
 
• The following are some of the provisions that can be altered in this manner: (i)** Fundamental Rights**; ii)** State Policy Directive Principles**; and (iii)** any additional regulations **that fall outside of the first and third categories.
 
 
 
• **Amendment by a special majority of the Parliament and the ratification of at least half of the state legislatures**: Amendments to the Constitution that pertain to the federal structure of the polity can be made by a special majority of Parliament and a simple majority of half of the state legislatures, respectively, with the consent of the other half. This modification is possible for the following **provisions**:
 
 
• The manner of the President's election.
 
• The extent of the states' and Union's executive authority.
 
• High courts and the Supreme Court.
 
• Legislative authority distribution between the Union and the states.
 
• any of the Seventh Schedule's lists.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendment Process**

 
 
• In order to initiate a constitutional amendment, a bill must be introduced in either **House of Parliament** (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha), not in the state legislatures.
 
• The bill does not require the president's prior approval to be introduced by a **minister or private member.**
 
• A special majority—that is, a majority of more than 50% of the House's total members and a majority of two-thirds of the House's present and voting members—is required for the bill to be approved in each House. The **bill** must be passed separately by **each House**.
 
• There is no provision for holding a joint session of the two Houses for the purpose of deliberation and bill passage in the event of disagreement.
 
• A simple majority, or a majority of the House members present and voting, is required for the bill to be **ratified by the legislatures** of half of the states if it aims to amend** federal Constitutional provisions.**
 
• The bill is presented to the president for approval after being approved by both Houses of Parliament and ratified, if necessary, by state legislatures.
 
• The bill needs the **president's approval.** After receiving the president's assent, the bill becomes an Act—also known as a** constitutional amendment act**—and the Constitution is amended in accordance with the terms of the Act. He cannot withhold his assent or return the bill to Parliament for reconsideration.

questions.question: Which of the following options correctly describes the features of arteries?

options.text: Thick walls, blood flows under low pressure, collect blood from different parts of the body
Thick walls, no valves, blood flows under high pressure, carry blood to different parts of the body
Thin walls with valves, blood flows under low pressure, collect blood from different parts of the body
Thin walls with valves, blood flows under high pressure, carry blood to different parts of the body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thick walls, no valves, blood flows under high pressure, carry blood to different parts of the body.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• **Blood **flows through the **arteries**.
 
• Most transport **oxygen-rich blood away** from the **heart **while delivering it **to **various **organs and tissues.**
 
• **Arteries **are a part of **circulatory system,** along with **heart **and the other blood vessels.
 
• The blood in arteries is typically **oxygenated**.
 
• As opposed to the **pulmonary artery**, which transports **deoxygenated blood **to the **lungs **for **oxygenation**, the pulmonary vein transports oxygenated blood back to the heart, where it is subsequently dispersed to rest of body through other arteries.
 
• Unlike arteries, which direct blood away from the heart, **veins **direct blood toward the heart.
 
• Because the arteries experience** higher pressures** than other blood vessels, they are often **thicker **and more **elastic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Normally, an artery has **three layers:**
 
• **Tunica intima:**
 
 
• The **innermost layer **of this layer is made up of elastic membranes and tissues that support healthy blood flow.
 
 
 
• ​**Tunica media:**
 
 
• This layer is the **middle **and thickest.
 
• There is **elastin **and **smooth **muscle.
 
 
 
• **Tunica adventitia: **
 
 
• Elastin and collagen fibres make up the tunica adventitia, which adds **strength**.
 
• This layer also enables the **dilation **and **widening **of **arteries**, which is essential for controlling blood pressure.
